proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2021` -- the PER-ISSUE DETAIL, PDF pages 43 and 45 of the FY2021 annual town report (printed folios 42 and 44). Fourteen debt issues against twenty-six fiscal years, FY2022 to FY2047: PDF p43 prints FY2022-FY2036 and PDF p45 prints FY2037-FY2047 plus a per-issue TOTAL column, which is read in the sibling group `fy2021-p45-debt-totals-by-issue.csv`. The GRAND TOTAL block these columns foot to is on PDF pages 44 and 46 and was proved independently by `fy2021-p44-debt-schedule.csv`. READ, NOT RECOGNISED: pdfplumber returns 0 words on both pages, and Vision's TSV is read a HALF-TURN OUT (pdf_tables.looks_flipped is True on each) and drops whole issues -- four of the fourteen have no figures at all in it. So every figure here was read off a 6x render, with ambiguous cells re-cropped at ~13x. FOUR KINDS OF ASSERTION. (1) The identity every issue-year states about itself, principal + interest + admin fee = the issue's total for that year: 189 of 198 close EXACTLY and the nine that do not are ALL three-summand Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust rows and ALL out by exactly $1. (2) Each of the twenty-six years' four column sums against the GRAND TOTAL block on pages 44/46: every one of the 104 within $2. (3) Each issue's twenty-six-year sum against the TOTAL column printed on page 45: within $8. (4) The whole matrix against the printed GRAND TOTAL of the schedule, which is the `kind=total` row here. THE TOLERANCE IS $21 AND IT IS DECLARED FOR 198 TERMS OF ROUNDING, not for a doubtful digit. The schedule prints WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts carrying cents, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts; 198 terms at half a dollar each is a worst case near $99. WHAT SAYS ROUNDING RATHER THAN A MISREAD IS THE CONTRAST: PRINCIPAL -- bond principal, which has no cents -- ties EXACTLY at $41,885,307 across all 198 cells, while interest is out by $20 and the MWPAT admin fees by $4. A misread digit in these figures costs at least $1 and almost always $100 or more, and it could not hide: every bond cell sits in a two-summand identity that closes to the dollar AND in a year column that ties to an independently proved page within $2. ONE CELL WAS SETTLED BY THE PAGE 44 COLUMN TOTAL AND IS WORTH NAMING: DPW-ROADS GENERAL OBLIGATION, FY2024. The glyph after the first digit is a filled bowl that reads as 0 or 8 in both the interest cell and the total cell, and BOTH readings close the row ($250,000 + $30,300 = $280,300 and $250,000 + $38,300 = $288,300). The FY2024 interest column total on page 44 requires $38,300, and at ~13x the glyph has the pinched waist of an 8. Read as $38,300 / $288,300.
